title: Jackson–Yoshimoto's spanning even tree conjecture for regular nonbipartite graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite connected graph, possibly with multiple edges but no loops. A spanning tree $T$ of $G$ is **even** if all leaves of $T$ belong to the same part of the bipartition of $T$. **Jackson–Yoshimoto's conjecture.** Every regular nonbipartite connected graph has a spanning even tree.

The conjecture asserts the existence of such a tree without the additional 2-factor hypothesis in the partial result preceding it. It is resolved by the paper's result that every connected graph that is not a regular bipartite graph has a spanning weakly even tree; in particular, every regular nonbipartite connected graph has a spanning even tree.
source_name: Jiangdong Ai, M. N. Ellingham, Zhipeng Gao, Yixuan Huang, Xiangzhou Liu, Songling Shan, Simon Špacapan and Jun Yue, “Spanning weakly even trees of graphs”, arXiv:2409.15522 (2024).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2408.07056](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.07056).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15522

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2024); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)
